vignette: Rahul, a 68-year-old South Asian man with a background in non-profit work, has found himself struggling to cope with the memories and emotions stemming from a traumatic event that occurred several years ago. Rahul was raped during an evening walk home from his office. This harrowing experience left him grappling with intense fear and anxiety ever since. In the aftermath of the incident, Rahul's world turned upside down. He vividly remembers the feeling of being helpless and overwhelmed by fear as he tried to fend off his attacker. Since then, he has been tormented by intrusive thoughts and images that replay the traumatic event, often jolting him awake at night in a cold sweat. These nightmares are so vivid that they feel like a reenactment of the trauma itself. Rahul finds himself avoiding certain areas near where the incident took place, especially during the evening hours when it happened. He has also become increasingly anxious about going out alone and often needs his daughter to accompany him for even minor errands. This avoidance extends to social gatherings; he is reluctant to leave home, fearing another similar encounter. His work at a non-profit organization, which he once found fulfilling, now seems overwhelming. Rahul reports that the stress of returning to his office can feel paralyzing. He often feels on edge and hyper-vigilant, constantly scanning for potential threats, even when surrounded by colleagues in familiar settings. This heightened state of alertness has made it difficult for him to concentrate on his job tasks, affecting both his performance and his sense of self-efficacy. The trauma has also strained his interpersonal relationships. Rahul’s divorce was finalized a few years ago, but he still feels a deep sense of isolation and disconnection from the world around him. He used to enjoy sharing stories about his work with friends and family over dinners or meetings, but now finds himself withdrawing into silence, unable to discuss the events that have deeply impacted his life. Rahul often describes feeling “numb” and disconnected from others. This emotional detachment is especially noticeable in conversations where he might otherwise share personal experiences or express emotions. He feels like a shadow of his former self, with a sense of hopelessness about ever recovering his previous level of engagement and joy in daily activities. At work, Rahul struggles to maintain his usual enthusiasm for the causes he once championed so passionately. The mission-driven nature of non-profit work has always been important to him, but now it feels like an insurmountable burden rather than a source of fulfillment. He finds himself questioning whether he can continue in this role, given the toll that re-experiencing his trauma takes on his mental health. Rahul also reports frequent outbursts of anger and irritability, which have strained his relationship with his daughter. She has noticed his withdrawal from family gatherings and the sharpness in his tone when discussing plans to go out or attend events together. He feels guilty about how his behavior affects her but is unable to control these reactions. In moments of solitude, Rahul questions whether he will ever be able to reclaim a sense of normalcy or peace. The trauma continues to color his perceptions and interactions, leaving him with an underlying fear that the safety he once took for granted no longer exists. Despite this struggle, there remains a glimmer of hope within him—a desire to find a way through the pain and rebuild his life. Rahul’s journey has been marked by resilience in the face of overwhelming adversity, yet the road ahead feels fraught with challenges. His experiences continue to shape how he navigates daily life, seeking small moments of solace amidst the ongoing struggle with trauma.
